abstract: We propose Pseudo Multi-Labels for single-positive multi-label (SPML) learning, a setting where each image has only one confirmed positive label and the remaining labels are unknown. The method trains a teacher network on SPML annotations and then uses the teacher's predictions as pseudo ground-truth labels to train a student network on fully labeled images. This simple self-training approach helps recover missing supervision and improves multi-label classification performance, with the student model approaching the performance of a model trained on fully annotated data.

abstract: This paper proposes a safety-critical obstacle avoidance control approach for autonomous surface vehicles (ASVs) with disturbances and uncertainties. Existing exponential control barrier functions (ECBFs) are extended to handle unknown disturbances, leading to input-to-state safe exponential control barrier functions (ISSf-ECBFs). An extended state observer is used to estimate unknown external marine disturbances and internal model uncertainties, and an anti-disturbance controller is designed accordingly. Based on the proposed ISSf-ECBFs, a quadratic programming problem is formulated to determine the optimal control input. The closed-loop system is proven to be input-to-state safe and uniformly ultimately bounded. Simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

abstract: 3D perceptual representations are well suited for robot manipulation as they encode occlusions and simplify spatial reasoning. However, many manipulation tasks require high spatial precision in end-effector pose prediction, which often demands expensive high-resolution 3D feature grids. We introduce Act3D, a manipulation policy transformer that represents the robot workspace using a 3D feature field with adaptive resolutions based on the task. The model lifts 2D pre-trained features to 3D using sensed depth, attends to sampled 3D points, and uses coarse-to-fine point sampling with relative-position attention to efficiently compute high-resolution 3D action maps. Act3D achieves state-of-the-art performance on RLBench, improving over prior 2D multi-view and 3D policies while using less compute. Ablations quantify the impact of spatial attention, large-scale vision-language pre-trained backbones, and weight tying across coarse-to-fine attention stages.

abstract: Monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO) is a critical problem in robotics and autonomous driving. Traditional methods solve this problem with filtering or optimization, but they often require manual tuning. Learning-based approaches can be end-to-end, but they typically rely on large models with many parameters and limited interpretability. We propose a fully differentiable and interpretable bird-eye-view (BEV) based VIO model for robots with local planar motion that can be trained without deep neural networks. The method uses an Unscented Kalman Filter as a differentiable layer to estimate pitch and roll while learning the noise covariance matrices, applies differentiable camera projection to generate gravity-aligned BEV images, and then uses a differentiable pose estimator to recover the remaining motion, yielding 5-DoF pose estimation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that the proposed approach is competitive with state-of-the-art methods and generalizes well to unseen scenes.

abstract: Robotic manipulation can benefit from the data efficiency, robustness, and predictability of model-based methods if robots can quickly generate models of novel objects. This is difficult when complex joint friction lacks clear first-principles models and when numerically stiff contact dynamics make standard model-building approaches struggle. We propose a method to simultaneously learn contact and continuous dynamics of a novel, possibly multi-link object by observing motion through contact-rich trajectories. Our method formulates system identification as a loss that infers unmeasured contact forces while penalizing violations of physical constraints and laws of motion under the current model parameters. Unlike prediction-based losses used in differentiable simulation, the proposed objective learns dynamics more directly. Using a new dataset of real articulated object trajectories and an existing cube toss dataset, the method outperforms differentiable simulation and end-to-end alternatives while using less data.

abstract: Colonoscopy is a key screening tool for colorectal cancer, but automated polyp segmentation methods often struggle with real-time performance and generalization across centers. We propose TransNetR, a transformer-based residual encoder-decoder network for colon polyp segmentation that uses a pre-trained ResNet50 encoder, three decoder blocks, and a final upsampling layer. On the Kvasir-SEG dataset, TransNetR achieves a Dice score of 0.8706 and an IoU of 0.8016 while maintaining real-time inference speed. We further evaluate the model under out-of-distribution conditions on PolypGen and two additional polyp segmentation benchmarks, showing strong generalization across multiple centers and state-of-the-art performance in these tests.

abstract: Robots are well-suited to alleviate repetitive and tedious manipulation tasks, but many applications require handling a wide variety of objects that are difficult to pre-program with fixed visual classifiers. We study learning a visual object classifier from a few human-provided examples by learning representations that distinguish the desired object category from others. Our approach integrates human supervision into contrastive representation learning with an additional loss that pulls human-selected examples close together in latent space. Experiments show improved performance over self-supervised and fully supervised baselines in offline evaluation, and the method also works in real time on a simplified recycling robot task with diverse objects.

abstract: Link prediction is a core task in graph learning with broad practical applications such as friend recommendation. Recent models commonly use either Dot Product or HadamardMLP decoders to score candidate edges from node embeddings. After theoretical and empirical analysis, we find that HadamardMLP decoders are generally more effective for link prediction, but they lack scalable top-neighbor retrieval on large graphs. To address this, we propose Flashlight, a sublinear algorithm that accelerates top scoring neighbor retrieval for HadamardMLP by progressively applying approximate maximum inner product search with adaptively adjusted query embeddings. Experiments show that Flashlight improves link prediction inference speed by more than 100x on the OGBL-CITATION2 dataset without sacrificing effectiveness, enabling large-scale applications with more effective decoders.

abstract: We study fairness in the context of feature-based price discrimination in monopoly markets. We propose a new notion of individual fairness, namely, alpha-fairness, which guarantees that individuals with similar features face similar prices. First, we study a discrete valuation space and give an analytical solution for optimal fair feature-based pricing. We show that the cost of fair pricing, defined as the ratio of expected revenue under optimal feature-based pricing to that under optimal fair feature-based pricing, can be arbitrarily large in general. When the revenue function is continuous and concave with respect to prices, we show that one can achieve a cost of fairness strictly less than 2, irrespective of the model parameters. Finally, we provide an algorithm to compute a fair feature-based pricing strategy that achieves this cost of fairness.

abstract: Searching for a path between two nodes in a graph is a fundamental problem across domains such as robotics, AI, and biology. We present PHIL (Path Heuristic with Imitation Learning), a neural architecture and training algorithm for discovering graph search and navigation heuristics from data by combining imitation learning with graph representation learning. PHIL trains a specialized graph neural network-based heuristic on search trajectories and shortest-path distances using backpropagation through the path-finding process. The learned heuristic produces graph embeddings useful for inferring node distances, runs in constant time with respect to graph size, and can be integrated with algorithms such as A*. Experiments show that PHIL reduces explored nodes by 58.5% on average over benchmark datasets and transfers across diverse graph domains, including biological networks and road networks.

abstract: Skill-based reinforcement learning (RL) leverages prior knowledge for accelerated robot learning by extracting skills from expert demonstrations and embedding them in a latent action space for a high-level RL agent. However, broad skill spaces make exploration difficult and can limit transfer to tasks structurally similar to those used to build the skills. We propose a state-conditioned generative skill prior to bias exploration toward skills relevant to the current robot state, together with a low-level residual policy for fine-grained skill adaptation. We validate the approach on four challenging manipulation tasks that differ from those used to construct the skill space, showing faster exploration and improved performance over prior work.

abstract: Mammograms are vital for detecting breast cancer, but low-quality scans and imaging artifacts can compromise downstream analysis. We introduce an automated pipeline to filter low-quality mammograms from large datasets. The pipeline is intended to support cleaner mammography datasets and is released as open-source software.

abstract: Bayesian optimisation is widely used to optimise stochastic black-box functions, but many applications require risk-averse objectives that account for distribution tails. We propose variational models for Bayesian quantile and expectile regression that are well suited to heteroscedastic noise settings. Our models use two latent Gaussian processes to represent the conditional quantile or expectile and the scale of an asymmetric likelihood. We also propose Bayesian optimisation strategies based on max-value entropy search and Thompson sampling that can directly optimise quantiles and expectiles without replicated observations or a parametric noise model. Experiments show that the proposed approach outperforms existing methods in heteroscedastic, non-Gaussian settings.

abstract: Stochastic gradient descent is widely used to optimize deep neural networks, but its gradient estimates can be noisy and unstable, which can slow convergence and hurt performance. We propose Filter Gradient Descent (FGD), a family of stochastic optimization algorithms that estimates the local gradient by solving an adaptive filtering problem over historical gradients. By incorporating past states, FGD reduces gradient variance and improves estimation quality. Experiments on numerical optimization and neural network training show that FGD is more robust than traditional momentum-based methods and can improve optimization performance.

abstract: There is emerging research interest in addressing the online 3D bin packing problem (3D-BPP), which has wide applications in logistics. However, neither heuristic methods nor deep reinforcement learning (DRL) methods outperform human packers in real logistics scenarios. One important reason is that humans can correct inappropriate packing actions by unpacking incorrectly packed items. Inspired by this unpacking mechanism, we present a DRL-based packing-and-unpacking network (PUN) to learn the synergies between these two actions for online 3D-BPP. Experimental results show that PUN achieves state-of-the-art performance, and the supplementary video demonstrates that the system can reliably complete the online 3D bin packing task in the real world.

abstract: A robot operating in a partially observable environment must perform sensing actions to achieve a goal, such as clearing objects in front of a shelf to better localize a target object and estimate its shape for grasping. A POMDP is a principled framework for enabling robots to perform such information-gathering actions. However, while robot manipulation domains involve high-dimensional and continuous observation and action spaces, most POMDP solvers are limited to discrete spaces. Recent work on POMCPOW extends online planning to continuous POMDPs using sampling and progressive widening, but it remains too slow for manipulation problems with camera observations and multiple objects. We propose a framework that learns to guide POMCPOW from past planning experience using preference learning over success and failure trajectories, with preference labels derived from tree-search results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in several continuous partially observable robotics domains, including real-world manipulation, where the method explicitly reasons about uncertainty in off-the-shelf segmentation and pose estimation algorithms.

abstract: We propose a bootstrap-based online algorithm for stochastic linear bandit problems. The method, LinReBoot, uses residual bootstrap exploration to estimate the next-step reward by resampling residuals from the mean reward estimate and selecting the arm with the highest estimated reward. We develop a theoretical framework to explain residual-bootstrap exploration in stochastic linear bandits and show that the resulting optimistic behavior yields a high-probability sublinear regret bound under mild conditions. Experiments demonstrate that LinReBoot is computationally efficient, generalizes well across linear bandit formulations, and performs competitively with existing methods such as Linear Thompson Sampling, Linear PHE, Linear GIRO, and Linear UCB.

abstract: Robots in complex multi-agent environments must reason about observed and unobserved agents under partial observability. We present Active Visual Planning (AVP), a learning-based method for prediction and planning that uses high-dimensional observations to learn a flow-based generative model of multi-agent joint trajectories, including agents that may be revealed in the future depending on the robot's actions. The model is trained offline from recorded observations rather than ground-truth states and supports contingency planning over the possible existence, intentions, and positions of unobserved agents. We demonstrate AVP in autonomous driving environments inspired by real-world scenarios, where it achieves expert-level closed-loop performance and outperforms methods that do not explicitly reason about unobserved agents.

abstract: Self-supervised learning can learn data-driven representations without annotations and is especially valuable in medical imaging where labels are scarce. We also extend ViT-AE++ to volumetric data. Experiments on natural and medical images show consistent gains over vanilla ViT-AE and strong performance relative to other contrastive learning approaches.

abstract: In this work, we present a scalable reinforcement learning method for training multi-task policies from large offline datasets that can leverage both human demonstrations and autonomously collected data. Our method uses a Transformer to provide a scalable representation for Q-functions trained via offline temporal-difference backups. We therefore refer to the method as Q-Transformer. By discretizing each action dimension and representing the Q-value of each action dimension as separate tokens, we can apply effective high-capacity sequence modeling techniques for Q-learning. We present several design decisions that enable good performance with offline RL training, and show that Q-Transformer outperforms prior offline RL algorithms and imitation learning techniques on a large, diverse real-world robotic manipulation task suite.

abstract: Dynamic network flow models have been extensively studied and widely used to formulate real-world control problems such as transportation, supply chain management, and power grid control. However, existing time-expansion and optimization-based methods struggle to scale to large dynamic networks and are limited in handling stochastic, nonlinear, or unknown dynamics. We present a graph network-based reinforcement learning framework for dynamic network control that combines data-driven decision making with problem-structured optimization. Our method uses a two-phase decomposition: first, an RL agent specifies desired outcomes for actions; second, a convex optimization step achieves these outcomes as well as possible under the network constraints. This formulation improves scalability and performance while retaining strong solution quality. We also study design choices, highlight useful system properties, and present experiments demonstrating the utility, scalability, and flexibility of the proposed framework.

abstract: This paper explores training medical vision-language models (VLMs), where visual and language inputs are embedded into a common space, with a particular focus on scenarios where training data is limited, as is often the case in clinical datasets. We explore several candidate methods to improve low-data performance, including: (i) adapting generic pre-trained models to novel image and text domains; (ii) using local and global contrastive loss functions, as well as combinations of the two; and (iii) adding extra supervision during VLM training through image- and text-only self-supervision and by creating additional positive image-text pairs through augmentation and nearest-neighbour search. Using text-to-image retrieval as a benchmark, we evaluate these methods with variable-sized training datasets of paired chest X-rays and radiological reports. Combined, they significantly improve retrieval compared with fine-tuning CLIP, roughly equivalent to training with 10x the data. Similar gains are found in downstream classification of CXR-related conditions, where our method outperforms CLIP and BioVIL in zero-shot and linear-probing settings. We conclude with recommendations for researchers training vision-language models on other medical imaging modalities when training data is scarce, and we release our code to support further research.

abstract: Existing imitation learning work usually assumes that the demonstrator and imitator share the same dynamics, which limits the use of demonstrations collected from other agents or robots. We study out-of-dynamics imitation learning (OOD-IL), where the demonstrator and imitator share the same state space but may differ in action space and dynamics. This setting introduces multimodal demonstrations and the challenge that some demonstrations are not transferable to the imitator. To address this, we propose a sequence-based contrastive clustering method to group demonstrations by mode, followed by an adversarial-learning-based transferability measurement within each cluster. Experiments on MuJoCo environments, a driving environment, and a simulated robot environment show that the proposed method better identifies non-transferable demonstrations and improves final imitation learning performance.

abstract: The cornerstone of neural algorithmic reasoning is the ability to solve algorithmic tasks that generalise out of distribution. While recent work has improved this area, it has largely focused on specialist models. Here we instead develop a generalist neural algorithmic learner: a single graph neural network processor that can learn to execute a wide range of algorithms, including sorting, searching, dynamic programming, path-finding, and geometry. Using the CLRS benchmark, we show that generalist algorithmic learners can be built by incorporating knowledge from specialist models. We present improvements to the input representation, training regime, and processor architecture that raise average single-task performance by more than 20% over prior work, and we study multi-task learning with these improvements. The results demonstrate a generalist learner that effectively transfers knowledge captured by specialist models.

abstract: This study assesses the knowledge and attitudes of medical students and doctors at the University of Ilorin toward artificial intelligence (AI) in medical education. Using a cross-sectional online survey of 481 respondents, the study found that most participants learned about AI from the media rather than from the medical school curriculum. Respondents who learned AI basics during medical school showed greater knowledge and interest in AI applications in healthcare. The study also found that AI influences specialty choice for some students, while attitudes toward being assessed by AI were mixed despite perceptions that AI-based assessment may be more objective.

abstract: We introduce PRISM, a method for real-time filtering in a probabilistic generative model of agent motion and visual perception. Previous approaches either lack uncertainty estimates for the map and agent state, do not run in real-time, do not have a dense scene representation, or do not model agent dynamics. Our solution reconciles all of these aspects. We start from a predefined state-space model that combines differentiable rendering and 6-DoF dynamics. Probabilistic inference in this model amounts to simultaneous localisation and mapping (SLAM) and is intractable. We use a series of approximations to Bayesian inference to arrive at probabilistic map and state estimates. We take advantage of well-established methods and closed-form updates, preserving accuracy and enabling real-time capability. The proposed solution runs at 10Hz real-time and is similarly accurate to state-of-the-art SLAM in small to medium-sized indoor environments, with high-speed UAV and handheld camera agents (Blackbird, EuRoC, and TUM-RGBD).

abstract: Recent advances in computer vision often rely on large models trained on vast amounts of labeled or unlabeled data, which can be difficult to use in resource-constrained settings. We present Astroformer, a hybrid transformer-convolutional architecture for galaxy morphology classification that is designed to work well in low-data regimes. The model combines a new network stack design, a modified relative self-attention mechanism, and carefully chosen data augmentation and regularization. On the Galaxy10 DECals dataset, Astroformer achieves 94.86% top-1 accuracy and sets a new state of the art, and it also improves results on CIFAR-100 and Tiny ImageNet. Our experiments suggest that methods tuned for large datasets do not necessarily transfer well when data is limited.

abstract: We propose SCALE, an approach for discovering and learning a diverse set of interpretable robot skills from a limited dataset. Rather than learning a single skill that may miss important modes in the data, we identify different modes through causal reasoning and learn a separate skill for each one. SCALE associates each mode with a set of causally relevant context variables discovered by causal interventions in simulation, enabling data partitioning by causal process and training compressed skills that ignore irrelevant variables. We model each robot skill as a Regional Compressed Option linked to a local causal process and its relevant variables. We demonstrate the approach on block stacking and peg-in-hole insertion under uncertainty, and show that the learned skills are compact, robust to domain shift, and suitable for sim-to-real transfer.

abstract: We present a seeing-eye quadruped navigation system that is robust to external human tugging forces and can estimate the direction and magnitude of those forces during blindfolded co-navigation. The method jointly trains a locomotion controller with reinforcement learning to remain stable under perturbations and a force estimator with supervised learning using onboard sensors only. At deployment, the estimator detects human tugs from joint encoders and IMU measurements, and the resulting force estimates inform global navigation decisions while a local planner handles obstacle avoidance using LIDAR. We evaluate the system in simulation and on a real quadruped robot, showing robust locomotion under external forces, accurate force-direction detection, and a full hardware demonstration with a blindfolded human.

abstract: Large language models have shown strong performance across many tasks, but their ability to understand concepts remains important for trustworthy use in real-world settings. This paper studies concept understanding in LLMs, focusing on abstract versus concrete concepts. The authors construct a WordNet-based dataset, D-Concept, and evaluate six pretrained language models on the hypernym discovery task. The results show that performance on abstract concepts is consistently worse than on concrete concepts, and that performance generally improves with model scale.
